title: Global historical imagery and frame-by-frame leads for Vatican/Rome research

scope.objective: Discover original imagery and moving-image frames; download only where accessible and licensed; georeference only with verified ground control points and documented error.

importantMethodNote: A global archive's existence does not establish that it contains a Vatican frame. Every candidate must be checked for exact footprint, capture date, original source, rights, and image quality. Oblique aerial photos and film frames are not orthophotos and cannot be accurately placed with a simple world file.

georeferencingChecklist: Download the original full-resolution file, not only a thumbnail or watermarked preview; preserve its source URL and checksum.
Read metadata and license; keep acquisition date separate from archive cataloguing, scan, upload and publication dates.
Classify image geometry: vertical aerial, oblique aerial, satellite frame, orthophoto, map, terrestrial panorama, drone video or indoor 3D scan.
For vertical aerial frames, use camera/flight metadata, DEM and appropriate orthorectification where possible.

For oblique photos and film frames, mark identifiable stable control points; use a projective transform only for a suitable planar approximation, and use photogrammetry/3D constraints if relief and perspective demand it.
Store each ground-control point with pixel x/y, longitude/latitude, CRS (WGS84/EPSG:4326 or explicit projected CRS), landmark description, source, and confidence.

Use at least 4 well-distributed control points for an initial projective fit, reserve independent checkpoints when possible, and report RMS/residual error. Do not fabricate coordinates or error values.
Export georeferenced GeoTIFF plus sidecar metadata and a footprint GeoJSON; retain the untouched original.
For video, record source URL, exact timecode, extracted frame index, checksum, and whether the frame is actually aerial; do not treat video frames as independent surveyed images.
Only publish a layer as georeferenced after inspecting its residuals and visual alignment against independent control features.

executionStatus.reason: The available runtime could not resolve external hosts for binary downloads, and the connected GitHub file interface supports text-file commits rather than binary raster upload.
executionStatus.reasonGeoreferencing: No original raster/video bytes or verified ground-control points were available in the execution environment; assigning a transform now would create false precision.
nextConcreteSteps: Use the linked official catalogues to identify and acquire original frames, especially AFN/ICCD, IGMI, NARA, ETH-Bibliothek and Istituto Luce.
For each acquired file, create a per-image metadata record and GCP file; run the documented GDAL/QGIS or image-matching workflow.
Publish only verified image footprints and error metrics to the map; leave unresolved candidates clearly marked as leads.

githubFindings.scope: Publicly indexed GitHub repositories, Gists, issues and technical discussions related to Vatican mapping, 3D data, imagery retrieval and georeferencing.
githubFindings.summary: Search surfaced a public Vatican boundary GeoJSON gist, a GitHub issue discussing IIIF retrieval for Vatican Museums catalogue images, a historical imagery downloader, and open-source photogrammetry tooling. No public evidence was found in these results of a verified stolen/hidden Vatican map or a repository run by a Vatican/Russian hacker containing georeferenced Vatican aerial frames.
githubFindings.safetyAndEvidence: Only public, lawful sources are included. Claims about hackers, nationality, or unauthorized access are not inferred from usernames or forum posts. Repository/tool availability does not establish that a particular image exists or has been downloaded.

latestVerifiedFindings.note: Istituto Luce catalogue confirms exact December 1950 aerial views of Vatican City/Rome. The catalogue records and image dimensions are verified from public index pages, but no binary original was downloaded in this run.
